threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it's weird to see someone busking with an accordion on a Tuesday afternoon at Dalston Junction.
Heard a couple argue about whose turn it was to pay for a kebab on the 36, while the driver pretended not to hear the chaos.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw my neighbor chasing after the BVG bus wearing slippers, yelling about missing the line 171. That's Neukölln life in action.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how the kebab shops here never close? It’s like they have a secret pact to fuel the night owls—best at 3 AM.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot locals by how they gauge BART delays—timing their coffee runs based on the latest equipment failures. Tourists just look confused.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in the back of the 49 bus playing a ukelele while a dog sat in a seat watching him like a fan. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always miss that Gràcia shuts down on Sundays; locals flock to the plazas instead, sipping vermut while shops rest. It's a whole different vibe.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their fascination with the 'paseo' culture—always blissfully unaware that the locals are just avoiding the heat.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused when the bus route changes mid-journey. Everyone else is just rolling with it like it's part of the experience.
Last night on the 47, the driver stopped for a cat crossing the road. Gave it a nod like they were old mates. Only in Bermondsey.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I found an old lady selling homemade jams under the S-Bahn bridge, chatting with regulars like it was the local pub.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You know you're in Kreuzberg when you see a group of guys playing chess on a traffic island. It's the unofficial sport of the block.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they know which BART delays mean they have to take the long walk to 16th instead of waiting for a train.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: The 31 Balboa had a guy trying to sell his mixtape—while we all crammed in like sardines. Only in SF do the morning commutes come with a soundtrack.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all locals love the Sagrada Família. Many of us avoid it—too many crowds and overpriced cafés nearby. Hidden gems are everywhere!

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They stand at the market prices, baffled by how cheap the fruit is, then treat themselves to overpriced avocado toast at a nearby café.
